Hook placement.
Event handler syntax.
State updates.

Props/data flow implementation.

sessions.title: Todo List with Filter
strengths: Identified that TodoProvider should own the todo state and todo modification functions.
Recognized that TodoInput needs access to the functions defined by TodoProvider.
Recognized the need for a mechanism to establish communication between TodoInput and TodoProvider.
Recalled the JavaScript spread syntax and connected it conceptually to creating a new array from existing state.
Used externalizing thoughts in writing to reason through component relationships.
struggles: Had difficulty clearly defining the role and responsibility of each component.
Had difficulty mapping the requirement that TodoInput access TodoProvider functions to the applicable React concept.
Knew React Context conceptually but struggled to identify when and how to apply it to the concrete problem.
Had difficulty reasoning about relationships between variables and components when given a clear set of requirements.
learned: React Context can establish communication between components when one component needs access to state or functions owned by another provider.
TodoProvider owns the todo state and operations while TodoInput owns the input interaction.
Context itself is not a component; it provides a communication mechanism that a provider supplies values through and consumers access.
React state arrays should be updated by producing a new array rather than mutating the existing array.
reinforce: React Context: createContext, Provider, and useContext.
Reasoning from requirements to component responsibilities.
Identifying which component owns state and which components need to consume or modify it.
Mapping concrete problems to applicable React concepts.
sessions.recurring_weakness: Difficulty reasoning about relationships between components, variables, and concepts when working from explicit requirements.
sessions.recurring_strength: Able to identify conceptual relationships and connect ideas when reasoning freely, especially after externalizing thoughts.

strengths: Successfully diagnosed and fixed the broken theme toggle
Completed the optional Footer stretch independently

struggles: Reverse engineering unfamiliar JSX syntax such as <ThemeProvider>{children}</ThemeProvider>

Distinguishing the ThemeProvider component from ThemeContext.Provider
learned: The Context Provider must expose every value or function that consumers need

The children prop contains the React elements placed inside a component
Object destructuring extracts properties from the props object
reinforce: React Context Provider and consumer relationships
sessions.recurring_weakness: Relational reasoning: understanding how concepts, components, and pieces of a system connect to one another
sessions.recurring_strength: Conceptual understanding improves when investigating the relationships between code elements after attempting a problem independently

sessions.title: Dynamic Welcome Message

Correctly recognized that initialName should determine the initial displayed name.

struggles: Did not know the React syntax for accessing and tracking an input element's value.
Initially attempted to access input.value without having a reference to the input element.
Initially confused the event handler parameter with the component's name state.
learned: A prop can be destructured from the props object using function parameter destructuring.
A whole props object can be accessed through property notation, while destructuring extracts selected properties.
An input value can be stored in React state so it can be accessed elsewhere in the component.
sessions.recurring_weakness: Relational reasoning and judging how concepts connect to one another
sessions.recurring_strength: Understanding conceptual relationships between React concepts
